text: Transmitters using the same technology, like in the previous examples, all of them were Wi-Fi access points. But it may also come from transmitters of different technologies. So for example, you have your Bluetooth, from your interface in your phone, and you like to receive the Bluetooth signal from your earphones. That's the useful signal, whatever. But there might be a Wi-Fi transmitter. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth may transmit exactly on the same frequencies, so they operate on the same frequencies. So this means that the Bluetooth receiver will get the Bluetooth, the standard Bluetooth signal fine, but overlapping with that, it will get also the Wi-Fi signal. That's power interfering power that is going to interfere with the useful signal. So we may get interference intra and inter technology. Intra is one is from the same technology, inter is one is from different technologies. But still, it's interfering power that we are getting, and in this metric, this interfering interfering signal goes to the denominator, along with the noise. So it's something nasty, something that lowers the quality of your communication. Good, so.
